tweets.text: BofA on CPI: "Beyond its implications for next week's Fed decision, we do not view the CPI report as particularly informative about the underlying inflation trend. The upside surprise was driven largely by core services, which increased 0.33% m/m. Within core services, wireless telephone services surged 5.9% m/m, contributing roughly 10bp to core CPI. The increase likely reflects AT&T's retirement of certain unlimited plans and higher administrative fees, which should prove to be a one-off. In addition, airfares and lodging away from home, two historically volatile categories, contributed a combined 8bp to core CPI. Airfares in particular may have been boosted by higher oil prices. These effects should prove temporary and largely unwind over coming months."

The Morning Minute (9.11)

⏰Top News:
-Crypto majors fall another 1-3% ahead of CPI; BTC at $76.9k
-BTC ETFs see $280M in outflows and $440M on the week
-Binance’s Bitcoin reserves hit 2-year highs
-Stonkfun ecosystem soars as Stonk hits $0.30 and multiple pairs run 2-4x+
-Robinhood Chain leaders rebound as volumes level off; Flycoin soars to $50M in its debut

🌎 Macro Crypto and Markets
-Crypto majors are red down 1-4%; BTC -1% at $77k; ETH -0.1% at $2,460; SOL -2% at $99; HYPE -4% at $79; ZEC -10% at $1,100
-Top alt movers include RAY (+16%), FF (+9%) and PONS (+6%)
-Oil +2% at $99; Gold -1% at $4,385
-Stock futures are green after oil sold off from highs; DOW +0.6%, Nasdaq +0.6%

-Senate Republicans released a revised 630-page Clarity Act ahead of a September 15 procedural vote, adding CFTC registration for “decentralized-in-name-only” protocols while leaving ethics provisions largely unchanged

-Sam Bankman-Fried petitioned the Supreme Court to overturn his fraud conviction, arguing he was barred from showing customers lost nothing and calling the $11 billion forfeiture an excessive fine

-Brian Armstrong told CNBC that $400,000 Bitcoin by 2030 remains a reasonable target, saying the year-long down cycle has bottomed and expecting SEC and CFTC guidance within weeks

-Binance's Bitcoin reserves topped 693,000 BTC, a two-year high and roughly 30% of major exchange reserves, after about 77,000 BTC moved onto the platform since late April

-Singapore's Alpha Ladder began distributing Payward's xStocks to institutional and accredited investors across selected APAC markets through its WealthX platform, following an MOU with Payward and MetaComp

-Ethereum developers tentatively set the launch date for Glamsterdam for Sepolia on October 6, though the upgrade hasn't run stably on any private devnet and no Hoodi or mainnet dates are fixed

Corporate Treasuries & ETFs
-The Bitcoin ETFs saw $283M in net outflows on Thursday; the ETH ETFs saw $30M in outflows

Meme Coin Tracker
-Meme leaders were red; DOGE -2%, SHIB -2%, PEPE -5%, PENGU -3%, TRUMP -3%, SPX -2%
-Robinhood chain leaders rebounded on the day; Pons +10% to $420M; AI +25% at $250M; Cashcat even at $160M; Flybrain +830%, Zforge 100x, Juggernaut +600% and Frong +100% led top movers
-On BSC, Niu Lau jumped 70% to $130M after its Binance spot listing; BREW +100% and Marscoin +20% were other top movers
-Solana top movers were led by Ember +165% and Fone +40%; Ansem -7% at $150M

-The Stonkfun ecosystem soared last night as STONK broke $0.30; Stonk +55% at $270M, ZCAT -7% at $83M, KNOTS +100% at $44M, BTC +94% at $18M and PURR +43% at $13M; LOOP +100x, METH +7x, LMEOW +180% , Stonkcat +7x and JUPCAT +6x led top movers

💰 Token, Airdrop & Protocol Tracker
-Hyperliquid led the onchain protocols with $2.08M in revenue on the day; PUMP was 7th with $1.4M, PONS next with $1.14M and Stonk was 13th with $760k
-Onchain RWA perpetual volume passed $120 billion in August, up from under $1 billion in October 2025, with open interest near $4.9 billion
-Raydium’s RAY token is up 86% this week on the back of its connection with the growing Stonkfun ecosystem

🚚 What is happening in NFTs?
-NFT leaders were mostly flat; Punks even at 30 ETH, BAYC -1% at 6.7 ETH, Pudgy -3% at 3.6 ETH
-Argonauts (+40%) and The 404 Machines (+20%) led top movers

US housing affordability is rapidly deteriorating:

This marks the 3rd consecutive monthly increase, totaling +$9,734.

By comparison, US median household income stands at $86,159 per year.

This brings the gap between median household income and the income needed to afford an average home to $38,515, the largest gap since July 2025.

This is just $2,288 below the $40,803 record set in June 2024.

To put this into perspective, median household income was $5,139 higher than the income required to buy a home in 2021.

Homeownership is becoming increasingly out of reach for the average American.

"In the old days, which is three years ago, we would see a company, and if what they were trying to do was too ambitious, we would not engage. Just too crazy, too complex."

"Implied by that is you wouldn't do a $100 million seed because it's too much money for almost any problem. It's too much money for any person to actually manage... It doesn't make sense as an inception round."

"Today we're almost seeing the opposite problem, where an idea that's too small is not something that we want to engage with."

"You can talk about how you put $100 million to work in a seed productively. I'm not recommending you raise $100 million, but this sort of no ceiling on ambition is showing up in how we're picking companies."

Leveraged funds are increasingly betting against tech stocks.

Britain is paying its wind farms almost £2 billion a year to switch off.

The grid cannot carry the power they generate, so the country pays them to stop spinning. These constraint costs have gone from a couple hundred million a year to over a billion in a decade.

Fixing it needs £70 billion, about $94 billion, four times the current pace of investment.

Building the turbines was the easy half. The wires are the bill, and it lands on your power bill either way.
